constraint_decided_it: Not a domain/range or FOL clause -- every property in both answers holds (P112/P113 E80->E18, P110/P111 E79->E18, P13 E6->E18, P108 E12->E24 with E22 subclass of E24, P33 E7->E29 with E12 subclass of E11 subclass of E7), and both correctly apply E80's redirect clause ('total decomposition ... such that the whole ceases to exist') to refuse E81. They separated on completeness against the case narrative and on evidence: B records the scrapped boiler's E6 Destruction (E6 scope note: 'If the matter remaining from the destruction is not documented, the event is modelled solely as an instance of E6 Destruction'), which is the event that actually bears on identity, and B resolves the functional-continuity objection with Velios' t1170 msg 11 ('not functional' as an observable phase property of industrial-heritage machines that 'used to perform a function ... but they no longer do') -- the exact case type here. A raises that same objection and leaves it unresolved at medium confidence.
better_modelling: The complete modelling is the union of the two, plus the carrier distinction neither drew: one continuing E22 (the engine); an E80 Part Removal, P112 diminished the engine / P113 removed the original boiler; a separate E6 Destruction, P13 destroyed the original boiler (matter not documented, so E6 alone, not E81); an E12 Production, P108 has produced the new boiler (E22) and P33 used specific technique the E29 Design or Procedure carried by (P128) the E31/E22 drawings in the county record office -- P33's own CRM example is 'The rebuilding of the German Reichstag (E11) used specific technique Architectural plans by Foster and Partners (E29)'; then an E79 Part Addition, P110 augmented the engine / P111 added the new boiler. No E81: E81's scope note itself excludes 'modifications (documented using E11 Modification) of objects that do not fundamentally change their nature or identity', and E80's own example is 'the removal of the engine from my car'. A omits the E6; B omits the E29/P33.
reasoning: Both answers reach the modelling the CRM prescribes and neither commits a domain, range, scope-note or FOL violation; all five distinct quotations (crm732#E80 'such that the whole ceases to exist'; t1170 'an instance of E19 with all parts replaced is identical', 'the continuity of functionality is broken', 'not functional') were checked against the sources and are verbatim, and B's note that Issue 369's outcome only transfers the Phase discussion to Issue 422 without ratifying Doerr's E19 remarks is accurate. Each is suboptimal for omitting one CRM-prescribed construct for an event the case states outright: A never records that the original boiler ceased to exist (E6 Destruction, P13), leaving a scrapped object still extant in the graph, while B never models the drawings as an E29 reached by P33 despite that being P33's paradigm case. B wins slightly because its omission is decorative and A's is load-bearing on the identity question asked, and because B answers the functional-continuity worry with in-thread evidence rather than, as A does, conceding it may cut the other way; B's one flaw is a clause attributing Doerr's new-object verdict 'precisely because the whole was disassembled', where Doerr's stated reason is that 'the continuity of functionality is broken'.
